title: feat: support speech-to-text (transcription) modality for community models
author: YoannDev90
pr_body_excerpt:
## Summary
- Adds a `transcription` modality to community endpoints (My Models): register an OpenAI-compatible upstream for `/v1/audio/transcriptions`.
- Enter: `/test` probes the endpoint with a sample audio file and reports `billableUsage.promptAudioSeconds`.
- Gen: `/v1/audio/transcriptions` proxies to the community upstream and attaches `x-usage-prompt-audio-seconds` + `x-model-used` usage headers.
- Billing mirrors first-party whisper/scribe: billed against `promptAudioPrice` (shared `promptAudioPrice` column) per audio second; duration read from `usage.duration` or `usage.seconds`, missing duration bills zero.
- Frontend: transcription option in the My Models dialog, base price key row, placeholders, fallback options.
- `normalizeCommunityEndpointInputModalities` now defaults transcription endpoints to `["audio"]` instead of `["text"]`.

## Tests
- Enter service probe tests (4): duration/seconds/zero/no-text.
- Gen unit tests (5): URL derivation, supported-endpoint restriction, definition/price, billing forwarding.
- Gen integration test: register → probe → gen transcription call → usage headers → `/audio/models` + `/v1/models` listing.
- `npx vitest run` on affected files green; typecheck green both services.

## Related
Fixes #13225

gist.headline: My Models learned to listen
gist.blurb: Community models can now lend the hive an ear. Register an OpenAI-compatible transcription endpoint, test it with sample audio, and turn spoken buzzing into text through the usual API.
gist.summary: Added a `transcription` modality for My Models, letting community OpenAI-compatible endpoints serve `/v1/audio/transcriptions` with per-second `promptAudioPrice` billing and audio-usage headers.
gist.impact: Developers can register, test, list, and call community speech-to-text models alongside first-party Whisper and Scribe, with `x-usage-prompt-audio-seconds` and `x-model-used` returned for each transcription.
